title: Asynchronous settlement callback gas exhaustion risk in is_settling guard
expected: Callback execution guaranteed or automatic timeout reset of is_settling flag
observed: If the follow-up step (on_settlement_payout) ran out of gas, is_settling stayed true and the payout's per-member deductions were never applied, so exits and settlements stayed refused for good. Measured live (E-CALLBACK-GAS-01, run 20261107T094616Z-259e): the step burns about 1.9 TGas plus 0.25 TGas per member (2.9 TGas for 4 members, 6.9 for 20, about 14 extrapolated to the 50-member maximum), so the flat 25 TGas gave about a 1.7x margin, not the 3.3x claimed earlier. The risk was real but small.
evidence: docs/lab-runs/20261107T094616Z-259e (E-CALLBACK-GAS-01: measured callback gas on testnet)
contracts/fly-coordinator/tests/unit_tests.rs (10 GAP-008 tests: pending record, no early recovery, permissionless recovery, late callback is a no-op, gas sized by members)
docs/lab-runs/20261107T095624Z-72b5 (E-CALLBACK-GAS-01 on the DEPLOYED fix, 24 of 24 assertions)
root_cause: Asynchronous cross-contract transfer promises allocate 20 TGas to callback which is sufficient for 50 flyers, but an unhandled callback out-of-gas condition would leave state locked
closure_condition: Show the floor live: a settlement attached with just enough gas still gets its follow-up step the sized allotment, and one attached with less is refused with nothing marked in flight
The recovery path can only be shown by unit test unless a test-only failure hook is added, which would change production code
resolution: Fix deployed and exercised on testnet without regression; the stuck path itself is covered by unit tests only.
fix: Two layers, built and unit-tested, DEPLOYED 2026-11-07 (tx ErUzdM1R4wH6yPeVTw4W98JRDdi5NZ6S5cWH3TRT233, code hash 6Jt4kSPXvzeoYBrqx3P576BJt5d1fxpHqiGSMtiDYX2n, 15 syndicates intact). (1) The follow-up step is given 25 TGas + 1 TGas per member (capped at 100): 75 TGas at 50 members, about 5x the measured need, and a settlement that cannot afford it is refused up front. (2) Each settlement records what its follow-up still has to do; recover_stuck_settlement lets ANYONE finish it 100 blocks after it started, charging members exactly as the follow-up would have, assuming the payout landed (assuming failure could let members withdraw money that has already left a contract that also holds other groups' funds). A late follow-up arriving after recovery changes nothing. Seven deliberate breaks of the new code are each caught by the tests.
also_noted: What live did NOT show: (1) the recovery path, because a follow-up step cannot be made to fail on purpose; (2) the gas floor: the run attached 250 TGas and unused gas also flows to the follow-up step, so it was allotted about 247 TGas, not the sized floor of 25 + 1 per member. The floor is shown by the unit test only. A caller that attaches little gas gets the floor; a caller that attaches a lot gets more. If a transfer really failed and the group was then recovered, that part stays in the contract and is not credited back to the members.
deployed_check: Live, on the fixed contract: 4-member and 20-member settlements ran, the follow-up step burnt 3.1 and 7.1 TGas (fit: 2.1 + 0.25 per member, about 14.6 at 50), logged success, and the pending record was gone afterwards.

title: The contract account pays for its own code and state from the same balance that holds escrow

observed: After the redeploy (larger wasm) the account had 0.095 NEAR of headroom; repeated lab runs added syndicate records and hatch failed with 'lacks balance for state'. closure_condition: Finished records can be removed and the run leaves no state behind

A live syndicate still costs more storage than the 0.01 NEAR hatch deposit while it exists; that is the price of being open, and it is returned when the record is pruned.

title: A partial settlement charged one member the whole payout and let the others exit with their full deposit
expected: After a settlement that pays out part of a syndicate's escrow, each member's recorded share falls in proportion to their deposit, so the members can only ever exit with what the syndicate still holds.
observed: balance * payout was computed in u128 with saturating_mul. For real amounts (0.05 NEAR x 0.10 NEAR = 5e45 yocto^2, above u128::MAX = 3.4e38) it clamped, every share became ~1.7e15 yocto, and the remainder 'dust' rule charged the entire payout to the member with the largest balance, capped at their balance. On testnet (run 20261105T033904Z-0c2a, syndicate cmp-mw2zxw34-c): four members deposited 0.05 each, 0.10 was paid out; member a was charged 0.05 and could not exit ('No escrow balance to refund'), while b, c and d each exited with 0.04999999830 NEAR, 0.15 in all against 0.10 NEAR left in the syndicate. The difference came from the contract's other balances. The unit and property tests used balances up to 1e7 yocto and never reached the overflow.
fix: DEPLOYED 2026-11-05 (tx 2fys41cS2cjo6TzAWx4X8ehu3pNXfH4jwXm7198WnK3C, code hash 9y8w4PU57V5GNd463J8DGa33xeZx8329MQdTFsbTHWJm). mul_div_floor: an exact 256-bit multiply-then-divide. Both new tests fail on the old code and pass on the new; 45 unit, 5 invariant and 6 integration tests pass. Built wasm hash 9y8w4PU57V5GNd463J8DGa33xeZx8329MQdTFsbTHWJm. Previous deployed hash: Gh8NAA2e78ETMMAWvExPnYfuKtRe2wQT2FHJ2RRXcPR9.
also_noted: calculate_max_payout multiplies the escrow by at most 10,000 bps with saturating_mul; it can only clamp above ~34 million NEAR in one syndicate. Not changed.
verified_live: E-CMP-INVEST-01 PASS on the fixed contract (run 20261105T035414Z-7a52): after a 0.10 payout from four 0.05 deposits every member exits with exactly 0.025. The full testnet tier (E-CHAIN-ROUND-LOCAL, E-IFACE-CHAIN, E-SECURITY-FCKEY-01, E-CMP-INVEST-01) passes (run 20261105T035644Z-7c1d).

title: Sealed bids are not authenticated to the NEAR account that deposited
expected: A bid is attributed to the account that placed it, so no one can bid or be charged in another member's name.
observed: submitSealedIntent takes a flyerId string from the caller and seals the bid to the Roost key, but nothing proves the caller controls that account. With per-member charges (settle_batch_charged) an impersonator could submit a bid under another member's id and have that member named a winner and charged. The harm is capped: the contract rejects a charge above the member's own deposit, the Roost rejects one above the bid it computed, and the fills (tokens) go to the named member, so the impersonator gains nothing directly; it is a griefing vector. With plain sums the same gap could only inflate a total, which the contract's policy bounds anyway.
closure_defined: Each sealed bid carries a signature by one of the account's NEAR access keys over (syndicate id, round nonce, ciphertext hash); the Roost checks the key belongs to the account (a view_access_key call from the room, or the contract verifying it) before accepting the bid.
evidence: docs/lab-runs/20261107T093948Z-2795 (E-SIGNED-INPUT-CHAIN-01, against the real testnet RPC)
docs/lab-runs/20261107T092049Z-2727 (E-TWO-ROOM-LIVE-01: signed inputs in four real rounds)
fix_built: 2026-11-07: signed sealed inputs (src/roost-service/signed-input.js, HostedRoost.submitSignedIntent): ed25519 signature by a key the chain says belongs to the account, bound to the round, with re-voting. E-SIGNED-INPUT-01 passes offline and is mutation-tested (10 of 10); the chain lookup was checked against testnet. Not yet closed: the auction and pool comparison experiments still use the unsigned path, and the Phala image does not contain the code.
fix: A sealed input is accepted only with an ed25519 signature, by a key the chain says belongs to the named account (full-access, or function-call limited to our contract), over the ciphertext and the open round (contract, syndicate, epoch, nonce), with a sequence number so a replay or stale input is refused. The lookup fails closed. A signed-only host refuses the unsigned path.
verified_live: E-SIGNED-INPUT-CHAIN-01 PASS: the account's own key accepted; a random key, another account's real key, a non-existent account and an unreachable chain are all refused. Four live two-host rounds used signed inputs with the real lookup.
also_noted: The comparison experiments of 2026-11-05 to 2026-11-07 (E-CMP-INVEST-01/02, E-CMP-AUCTION-01) used the unsigned path and said so; they were not re-run. The default HostedRoost still accepts unsigned inputs unless requireSignedInputs is set, and the Phala image does not yet contain the signed-input code.

title: The release cap bounds each settlement, not the pace of release, and a Dark Vault's exit timer restarts with every settlement
expected: A compromised host can release at most max_release_bps_per_epoch of a group per epoch, and members can always reach the exit within the timer.
observed: calculate_max_payout takes a share of the CURRENT total_escrow at each settlement, and the epoch advances once per settlement (not per period). On testnet (run 20261107T131007Z-d8a0, E-ONGOING-01 part B), with a key standing in for a compromised host and a 25% cap, a payout of 0.11 of 0.4 was refused, but payouts of exactly 25% of the current escrow succeeded back to back (0.1, 0.075, 0.05625), releasing 57.81% of the group within minutes against a stated 25% per epoch. Ten such settlements would release about 94%. In a Dark Vault each settlement also restarts the exit timer (measured: an exit right after round 3 was refused as 'Deliberation window still active' 65 blocks after the group opened), so a host that settles more often than the timer keeps members out while draining. The recipients allowlist still holds: money can only go to allowed recipients.
root_cause: The cap is a rate per settlement and an epoch is a counter, not a time window; no cumulative release or minimum spacing between settlements is tracked.
closure_condition: Track cumulative release per time window (a block-length epoch) or enforce a minimum spacing between settlements, without breaking existing syndicates' stored state (use separate storage keys, as the second-room key does)
Decide whether a settlement should restart the exit timer in a Dark Vault, or only a new time window
Re-run E-ONGOING-01 part B: three back-to-back 25% payouts must be refused after the first
resolution: Fixed and verified live; pacing is only as strict as the timer (GAP-025).
fix: DEPLOYED 2026-11-07 (tx DPbQ2944vhcHRF16EkML5djiYvvZ3oW1giNsZFaEAhUe, code hash DNZDmhLRfSubVSfNoHtAjRZaPLCpvchTSqeqJgxa4si1, 15 syndicates intact). A release window of twice the exit timer (timeout_blocks); within it the total released may not exceed cap x (escrow at the window's start + deposits since); a failed payout gives its allowance back; a Dark Vault's epoch and exit timer advance with a new window, not with every settlement; the window lives under its own storage key; get_release_window view. 14 new unit tests (106 in all); 11 deliberate breaks caught.
verified_live: E-ONGOING-01 re-run PASS (run 20261107T134236Z-af24, 73 assertions): 0.1 succeeded, a second 0.075 straight after and even 0.001 were refused, the allowance returned in a new window sized to the then-current escrow; a settlement inside a window did not advance the epoch or move the exit timer, and members exited 12 blocks before the old rule would have let them.
also_noted: The limit is only as strict as the exit timer: a window is twice the timer in real time. At the 24-block timer tested (a 27-second window) about 90% could still be released in nine windows, roughly four minutes; at a one-hour timer it would take about 18 hours. A real group must choose its timer on purpose. See GAP-025.

title: A group can be opened with a one-block exit timer, and the timer is not part of the policy hash depositors consent to
expected: Depositors consent to the pacing of release and the length of the exit wait.
observed: hatch accepts any timeout_blocks of 1 or more. The release window is twice that, so a group opened with a tiny timer has a window of a few blocks and the GAP-024 pacing is meaningless. The policy hash that depositors consent to covers the recipients, the cap and the deadline, not the timer, so a depositor must read timeout_blocks from the group's state before depositing; nothing binds it.
evidence: docs/lab-runs/20261107T142512Z-3f69 (E-IFACE-CHAIN, PASS, through the new deposit path)
root_cause: The timer was designed as an exit delay, not as a security parameter; the release pacing now depends on it.
closure_condition: Decide a minimum timer, or put the timer into the policy hash so depositors consent to it, or make clients refuse to deposit into a group whose timer is below a stated minimum
Test: a hatch below the minimum is refused, or a deposit with a hash that omits the timer is refused

resolution: Fixed in two layers. Contract: new groups are opened with a version-2 policy hash that includes the exit timer, so a deposit that leaves out or misstates it is refused; a timer below 10 blocks (about 6 s) is refused at hatch (a sanity floor, not a recommendation: choose the timer on purpose). get_policy_terms shows every group's terms and whether the timer is covered. Clients: deposit() needs a hash the caller computed or the terms it expects and never copies the contract's hash (a client that did would always pass the check). Remaining limits: the 15 groups opened before the change keep the old hash, so their timers are not covered (the view marks them); the check is in software, a person still has to read the terms; the floor is a minimum, not the right value for a group.

title: One bidder who cannot pay sank a whole charged round
expected: A bidder who cannot cover their worst case is left out and named; the rest settle.
observed: The contract refuses a charged settlement if any charge exceeds that member's escrow; the Roost turned every readable bid into a charge and kept no list of who had deposited, so one unfunded or short bidder made the contract reject the whole round (funds were never at risk; the round was lost and the queue already cleared). evidence: docs/lab-runs/20261108T103619Z-433a (E-ESCROWBOUND-01 offline x3, E-ESCROWBOUND-LIVE-01 testnet x3, all PASS, log verified; supersedes 20261108T081854Z-d13c, which ran the reader before the review fixes)

docs/lab-runs/20261108T124630Z-b8de (E-HOSTED-ESCROW-LIVE-01: inside a real Phala TDX VM, with the escrow settings in the measured compose file, the unfunded member was left out and the settlement landed on testnet)
root_cause: The Roost had no view of the contract's escrow.
closure_condition: Predictions committed first, tests first, mutation-checked, promoted live run
regression_guard: tests/hosted-roost-escrow.test.js, tests/escrow-reader.test.js, tests/room-service-escrow.test.js, tests/roost-server-escrow.test.js, labs E-ESCROWBOUND-01 and E-ESCROWBOUND-LIVE-01 (19 mutants killed)
resolution: bindEscrow reads, from two or more different providers at one final block (each provider vouches for the block by hash and every reply must come from it), what each bidder and each payer (a ballot's whole roll) holds; pool, auction, quote(lend), cross and rfq(sell) leave out bidders whose exact worst case exceeds their escrow (first/second-price auctions: price x the whole lot; uniform: price x units they can be filled; cross: units x the public reference price); quote(buy), rfq(buy) and payrun refuse (queue kept) if their one payer cannot cover its limit. Left-out members are named by account only and a ballot no longer reveals that one voted. The block is in the signed order hash (not payrun's published formula). Fails closed (UNAVAILABLE/503, queue kept); a read older than 30 s is refused; the whole read has a deadline and timed-out requests are aborted. IMPORTANT LIMIT: this makes a rejected round much rarer, NOT impossible. A member whose exit timer has run can still leave between the read and the payout, and the contract then rejects the round (no funds at risk). escrowBlock.raceFree is an ESTIMATE (the first block at which anyone could leave must be later than the read's block + its age at one block a second + the 30 s a read may be used + 30 blocks for the payout); it was false in the live run. Two-room settlements need a pinned block (escrowBlockHash) or the two rooms sign different messages. Not tested live: the race itself, providers that lie. Trusts the providers; two that must agree narrow that, they do not remove it. HOSTED: the escrow check is ON in the measured deploy/roost/docker-compose.yml (ROOST_RPC_URLS: two different providers; ROOST_CONTRACT_ID), so the attestation covers which providers the hosted Roost asks and which contract it reads. Verified live on an ephemeral TDX VM (deleted afterwards; none is running now): image cde03fef… attested, compose hash edd3ff37…, the VM read block 276777717 from the two providers through its own network, left out the unfunded member, signed, and the real contract accepted it. Still true: much rarer, not impossible (the exit race); raceFree was false; the attestation proves which providers are asked, not that they are honest; if both are down the hosted Roost refuses charged rounds with 503; the VM failing closed was not tested on hardware.

resolution: abandonSignedRound (service abandon, POST /v1/rooms/abandon, the Roost server's POST /abandon, the MCP tool midge_abandon_room_round and the SDK RoomsClient.abandon; coordinator only) clears the signed mark, drops the escrow read, and records the order hash, message hash, allocation and charge hashes and the signature (newest 100, in memory, LOST on restart; the public event stream carries only the order and message hashes). docs/lab-runs/20261108T170912Z-53f2 (E-MODEL-PIN-LIVE-01 PASS against the real NEAR AI host: measurements identical across three reads; the baseline accepted with the Intel chain verified and TCB UpToDate; a wrong value refused by field name for each of five fields; a list accepted)
docs/canonical/model-measurements.json (the baseline: what was observed, with a note that it has not been checked against anything NEAR AI publishes)
root_cause: The quote body was parsed only for REPORTDATA.
closure_condition: expectedMeasurements pin implemented, malformed pins throw instead of being ignored, tests first and mutation-checked
resolution: checkModelCandidate, selectVerifiedModelKey and fetchVerifiedModelKey take expectedMeasurements ({ field: [accepted 96-hex values] }, a list so a rotation can accept old and new). Each pinned field is compared; a mismatch fails the candidate and names the field. The result reports the measurements read and whether they were pinned. Nothing is pinned by default, on purpose: this repository cannot decide which build to trust. OPERATING SIDE, 2026-11-08: the pin is switched on with the environment setting MIDGE_MODEL_MEASUREMENTS (read by every caller of fetchVerifiedModelKey; an explicit expectedMeasurements wins and null turns it off; a malformed setting throws, naming the variable), and scripts/measure-model.js (npm run measure:model) reads the host several times with fresh nonces, reports whether the measurements held still, and prints a setting to paste, with the warning that the values are only what was observed. 12 tests (tests/model-measurement-pin.test.js), four mutants each caught. The real host was read read-only: the measurements were identical across reads. CLOSED 2026-11-08 on the owner's instruction: a tracked baseline of the five boot and runtime registers observed on the real host (docs/canonical/model-measurements.json), loaded by loadMeasurementBaseline (which refuses a file that does not say its values are only observed and not verified), and used by the live model check (scripts/verify-roost-model.js) unless --no-pin or MIDGE_MODEL_MEASUREMENTS is set. The library default is still no pin. What remains true: the baseline is a sighting, not NEAR AI's published build, and a new NEAR AI build is refused by a pinned caller until its values are added. AMENDED 2026-11-08: the live model check does not fail when NEAR AI ships a new build. attestAgainstBaseline pins the baseline, and a host that differs ONLY in its measurements is attested without the pin and a plain warning is printed; any other failed check still stops; --require-pin makes a mismatch a failure, --no-pin skips the comparison, and a MIDGE_MODEL_MEASUREMENTS the owner set is strict. 9 tests (tests/baseline-attest.test.js), four mutants caught; demonstrated on the real host with a deliberately wrong baseline (read-only, not a promoted run).

title: The hosted Roost image never requires signed inputs, so ballots, RFQs and pay runs are refused on the real Phala VM
surface: src/roost-service/server.js (entry point built HostedRoost without requireSignedInputs), deploy/roost/docker-compose.yml
expected: Every room program the docs describe (pool, quote, ballot, RFQ, pay run) runs on the hosted Roost on real hardware.
observed: Live run 20261111T043528Z-3f73 on a real TDX VM: round 1 (pool) passed; the ballot was refused with 'a ballot is only counted on a host that requires signed inputs'. The server entry point never turns signed inputs on. Ballots, RFQs and pay runs only worked against local rooms.
root_cause: server.js built the Roost with only an escrow reader; requireSignedInputs and its account-key check existed in HostedRoost but were not reachable from the environment.
closure_condition: roostFromEnv reads ROOST_REQUIRE_SIGNED_INPUTS=1 (done, tests/roost-server-signed-env.test.js)
a new image is built by CI from the merged code and pinned by digest in the compose file with ROOST_REQUIRE_SIGNED_INPUTS=1 and its new compose hash pinned in roost.expected.json
a live hosted run counts a ballot
required_verification: hosted lab run with a ballot round passes on a real VM
resolution: Fixed and rebuilt: CI image 0e09e816…3804d4 from the merged code, compose requires signed inputs. A real Phala TDX VM attested that compose and ran a signed-input ballot (run 20261111T050533Z-d6d9, PASS, VM deleted). Residual: RFQ and pay run on hardware not exercised (same mechanism); the account-key check asks one RPC provider.

title: A foreign payment reservation that never resolves locked the payee's budget forever (lifetime running total)
expected: A reserved obligation that is not resolved within a bounded number of blocks can be released by anyone, like the 100-block settlement recovery.
observed: request_foreign_payment records the obligation and reserves budget before the signer is called; only on_foreign_signed releases it. since_block is recorded but never read for foreign obligations, and there is no cancel for a signed payment that is never broadcast.
root_cause: The foreign-payment state was added with a reserve-then-callback design but without the recovery and cleanup the older settlement path has.
closure_condition: The running total is per window, so an unresolved reservation locks capacity for one window only
A late signer failure never reduces a later window's total
resolution: Fixed with a window (ForeignPolicy.window_blocks, at least 100). Correction recorded: the first proposed fix, letting anyone release an unresolved reservation after N blocks, would be unsound because the contract cannot see the other chain. Verified by unit tests and, for the window itself, live: E-FOREIGN-WINDOW-LIVE-01 run 20261111T094402Z-fb66 (the cap held inside a 100-block window, the allowance returned after it, the same request then landed on Solana devnet, and the first obligation id stayed burned). Residual, unit tests only: a late signer failure not reducing a later window's total.

title: prune_syndicate leaves the foreign policy, obligations and running totals behind
expected: Pruning a group removes everything stored for its id.
observed: prune_syndicate removes the group, its second key and its window but not f:<id>, fo:<id>:* or fs:<id>:*, so hatching the same id again inherits the old foreign policy and totals.
root_cause: The foreign-payment state was added with a reserve-then-callback design but without the recovery and cleanup the older settlement path has.
closure_condition: Pruning removes the foreign policy
A re-hatched id inherits no obligation or total
A stranger cannot prune a group that has a foreign policy
resolution: Fixed: policy slot removed on prune; obligation and total slots keyed to the group's creation block; owner-only prune when a foreign policy exists. Old entries remain in storage, unreachable. Verified by unit tests only.

title: A freed and re-hatched group id derived the same foreign addresses as the old group
expected: A group controls only the foreign money it was funded with; a freed group id cannot be used to take over an earlier group's foreign addresses.
observed: The signer path was exactly the group id, so the same contract and the same id always derived the same Solana and Ethereum keys. After a prune the id is free; anyone can hatch it with their own room key and foreign policy and pay out whatever the old group left at those addresses. Reported by a review note; confirmed by reading the code (the path was the id). The attack itself was not run.
root_cause: The foreign-payment feature built the signer path from the id alone. GAP-048's cleanup reset the books of a re-hatched id but not its addresses, which I wrongly described as 'starts clean'.
closure_condition: The signer path names the group's creation block
get_foreign_path exposes it
A re-hatched id gets a different path
required_verification: a live payment signed from an address derived from the path
resolution: Fixed: path is <id>:<created_at_block>. Verified by unit tests and live on the test copy (run 20261111T063342Z-0a0b) and on production (run 20261111T063548Z-dd0c): the signatures verify against addresses derived from that path. Consequence, stated: groups created before this build derived their addresses from the bare id; those addresses are no longer reachable by the contract (testnet dust). Money must be moved out of a group's foreign addresses before the group is pruned: after a prune nobody can sign for its path.

title: The fail-closed live test cannot run against the signed-only compose, and bid intake now depends on one RPC provider
surface: src/roost-service/server.js (roostFromEnv: the account-key check uses the first ROOST_RPC_URLS entry), lab/experiments/106-hosted-failclosed-live.js
expected: The fail-closed property (with the chain unreadable a charged round is refused with 503 and the queued bids survive) can still be shown live on the current compose.
observed: Run 20261111T094151Z-c01e on a real VM: the fixture attested, then the experiment's bid was refused with 'this Roost only accepts signed inputs', because the experiment sends an unsigned bid and the signed-only compose refuses it. Reading the code shows a second effect: with signed inputs required, accepting a bid needs the account-key check, which asks the FIRST provider only; with that provider unreachable no bid can be queued at all. So intake fails closed earlier than before (an availability cost) and rests on one provider for key checks (a trust and availability point), while escrow reads use two.
root_cause: Making the hosted room signed-only (GAP-046) added a chain read to bid intake that shares the first escrow provider, and the fail-closed experiment predates the decision.
closure_condition: Decide: give the key check its own provider list (more than one, which must agree, like the escrow reader) or accept and document one
Rewrite the fail-closed experiment to send signed bids and to show the property that still applies on the current compose
Rebuild the image and re-attest if the compose changes
required_verification: a hosted live run on the current compose showing a charged round refused and the bid kept, with signed bids
resolution: Fixed: the account-key check asks every configured provider and needs them ALL to confirm (a provider that says no or differs refuses the key, one that fails is an error); it has its own list, ROOST_ACCOUNT_CHECK_RPC_URLS, measured in the compose file; fewer than two different providers is refused at start-up. The fail-closed experiment now sends a signed bid and passed on real hardware on the signed-only compose (run 20261111T102056Z-1b53): the bid was accepted while both escrow providers were unreachable, the charged round was refused with 503 in 44 ms, the bid survived, and a wrong-key bid was refused. The pay run passed on the rebuilt image and the new compose (run 20261111T102349Z-a216) and its compose hash is pinned. Residual: the account-check providers failing is covered by unit tests only.

title: The contract source in the repository built to a different wasm than the production contract (a refactor with no behaviour change)
expected: The default build of the repository's contract source is byte-identical to the code on c.fly-1793636729.testnet, so anyone can rebuild and compare hashes.
observed: The default build of the current source hashes to 3dGAu1yG9gaZbMTXWX3eYjN8mVM2LUyQR8Czu9W1vg1C; production runs BVcq86Wz5Q3kcdBdcUhfQVfQtC6CmGwcXuMd52aW6gTp (built before the signer was moved into a helper function so that a test-only build could override it). The default build has no test methods (checked on the compiled wasm: no set_test_signer, no test:signer key) and the 174 Rust tests pass, but the bytes differ. The test copy m.fly-1793636729.testnet runs the new default build.
resolution: Fixed without a deploy. The pre-refactor source rebuilt to production's exact hash (BVcq86Wz…), so builds are reproducible on this machine and the drift was my refactor. The test-signer override was restructured: the original signer statement is untouched, only its use is wrapped (Promise::new(signer_override(signer))), and all new code sits at the end of the file, so no line number embedded in a panic location moves. The default build again hashes to BVcq86Wz…, the test copy runs it, and E-CHAIN-ROUND-LOCAL and E-IFACE-CHAIN pass again (run 20261111T164639Z-e8c8). 174 Rust tests pass by default and 2 with the feature; clippy is clean both ways.
verify: node lab/run.js --only E-CHAIN-ROUND-LOCAL (fails at its pre-flight if the local build is not the deployed code)

title: The hosted room's account-key check treated any reply that was not a clear yes as "not a key", so a rate-limited provider made it refuse every member's bid with a misleading message
expected: A provider that cannot answer is reported as such (and retried briefly); only a provider that clearly says the key does not exist makes it "not a key".
observed: Between 20:02 and 20:13 UTC three hardware runs failed with '[ROOST REJECT] ed25519:... is not a key of <member>': the escrow experiment (twice) and, as a control, the buy-side RFQ experiment that had passed at 12:31 on the same image and compose. The check returned false for any reply with a JSON-RPC error, so a rate-limit reply (code -429, the shape the free FastNear endpoint returns under load) became 'not a key'. A separate cause was reproduced from this machine: a freshly created account's key is shown by the FastNear provider several seconds after the other provider shows it, so a bid signed within about 20 seconds of account creation is refused. Run 20261111T201328Z-4418 (the control). After the fix was merged and the image rebuilt (digest sha256:3014e8f0…c38531, run 20261111T212638Z-cbf5 on a real VM), the refusal changed from 'is not a key' to 'could not check that … is a key of …': the fix works in the image, and it shows that from the VM at least one of the two providers cannot answer even after retries. The refusal did not say which provider or why.
resolution: makeAccountKeyCheck now returns false only when the provider says the key or account does not exist, retries a rate limit, HTTP error or missing result up to three times with a short pause, and then throws naming the provider, so the room reports 'could not check' and the cause is visible. A key is still never accepted without every provider's yes. The lab's member helper waits for the same agreement before using a new account. 12 key-check tests (5 new) and 462 JS tests pass; the logic was run against both real providers. NOT yet on hardware: the change is in the Roost image, so it needs the image rebuilt by CI on merge, its compose hash pinned and attested, and the hardware experiments re-run. Second step: the refusal now carries the provider's reason (for example 'b.example could not answer (-429 Rate limits exceeded)'), cut to 160 characters, so an operator can see which provider fails from the VM. Tested (3 tests, 465 JS tests pass). Still to do on hardware: rebuild, pin, attest, and read the reason; then choose providers the VM can reach.
